findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance's underlying EBS storage, snapshots, and automated backups are stored in cleartext. Any compromise of the storage layer or a shared snapshot exposes all database contents.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the MySQL service to untrusted networks and relying solely on the security group for protection. The db_endpoint output further advertises this address.
The master user is set to the predictable default 'admin', which combined with a publicly accessible endpoint makes credential brute-force/spraying attacks materially easier.

The master password is supplied through a plain Terraform variable rather than a managed secret (e.g. manage_master_user_password / Secrets Manager), so it is stored in cleartext in the Terraform state and likely in tfvars or CI variables.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so the database relies exclusively on a static shared master password with no centrally revocable, short-lived IAM token authentication.

No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit, error, general, slowquery) are configured, so authentication and query activity on an internet-exposed database is not retained for detection or forensic investigation.
skip_final_snapshot = true combined with backup_retention_period = 0 disables point-in-time recovery, meaning accidental or malicious deletion of the instance destroys all data with no recovery path.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving any principal that assumes the EC2 role full control of all S3 buckets, EC2 resources and RDS databases in the account. Since this role is attached via aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2profile to the aws_instance.db_app host, compromise of that instance (or SSRF against its metadata service) yields account-wide data access and a privilege-escalation path (e.g. ec2:RunInstances with PassRole-like abuse, modifying security groups, snapshotting RDS).

The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database/app security group, providing no outbound network boundary and enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host or database instance.

The database password (var.password) and username are interpolated in cleartext into the EC2 user_data script, which is stored unencrypted in instance metadata and retrievable by anyone or any process that can reach the IMDS endpoint (including via SSRF from the hosted PHP app) or who can call ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute.

No root_block_device/ebs_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance volumes holding the database credential file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) and application data are unencrypted at rest.

metadata_options is not configured, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled. Combined with an attached instance profile and a public-facing PHP application, a server-side request forgery could retrieve the role's temporary credentials.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the employee data form over plain HTTP only, with no TLS configuration, so submitted personal data and page content traverse the network unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: public IP exposure of app instance
findings.description: The instance is placed in a subnet named web_subnet and its public DNS is exported as an output, indicating it receives a public IP; associate_public_ip_address is not explicitly disabled, so the credential-bearing instance is directly reachable from the internet rather than fronted by a load balancer.
